solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Branch of science is obligatory and so complicated (12)

indicators.note: made complicated, the letters are tangled into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone grumbling that a compulsory science course is needlessly hard.
annotation.walkthrough: The complaint about a compulsory, difficult subject reads naturally, which hides that 'obligatory' and 'so' together hold exactly the twelve letters needed.
annotation.definitionFit: Astrobiology is the science of life beyond Earth, a branch of science.

entries.clue: Judge mishandled rare cases a little (7)

indicators.note: handled badly, so the letters of RARE are put out of order
the rearranged letters encase, or wrap around, the next piece

blocks.note: RARE rearranged, split AR…ER around the filling

annotation.surface: A judge who botched some rare cases, but only slightly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like a noun for a judge's lawsuits; here it is a verb, the jumbled RARE casing BIT: AR(BIT)ER.
annotation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone who judges or settles a dispute.

entries.clue: Residence in outskirts of third-rate French city (7)

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Someone living on the shabby edge of a French city.
annotation.walkthrough: Nancy is a city in north-east France; the outskirts are the outer letters of 'third-rate', not the suburbs of the city.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the occupation of a property as a tenant, a residence.

entries.clue: Immediately in a tricky situation (2-3-4)

blocks.note: first sense: at once, there and then, as a fine issued without delay
second sense: cornered, as when asked an awkward question in public

annotation.surface: Being caught out without warning.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses sit so close together that the clue reads as one phrase; split it after 'Immediately'.
annotation.definitionFit: On the spot means both at once and in an awkward position.

entries.clue: Fashionable rock fan’s last to leave metal bar (5)

indicators.note: the last letter departs from the word

blocks.note: GOTH, a fan of gothic rock, losing its last letter H

annotation.surface: A trendy rock fan making an exit from a heavy-metal bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Metal bar' conjures a heavy-metal pub for the rock fan; it is the definition, a bar of metal. A goth is a fan of dark gothic rock.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: gold and silver are cast into small bars for storage and trade.

entries.clue: Greek character embracing a sexy dance (7)

indicators.note: wrapping its arms around the next piece, so it goes inside

blocks.note: lambda, the Greek letter L, split LAMB…DA

annotation.surface: A Greek man clasping a partner in a sultry dance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person; it is a letter of the alphabet. LAMB(A)DA.
annotation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian dance famous for close, sensual moves.

entries.clue: Telling cooks to produce fishing gear (4,3)

indicators.note: to cook is to fiddle or doctor, so the letters are altered

annotation.surface: Instructing chefs to rustle up equipment for catching fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Telling cooks' reads as giving orders to chefs; 'telling' is the raw material and 'cooks' the instruction to jumble it.
annotation.definitionFit: A gill net is a fishing net that traps fish by their gills.

entries.clue: Top pilot owing money for America’s secret weapon (3,2,3,4)

blocks.note: an ace is a star fighter pilot

annotation.surface: A crack American pilot in debt, framed as the nation's hidden weapon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'America’s' flags that the definition is the US form of the idiom; the British say 'ace up one's sleeve'.
annotation.definitionFit: An ace in the hole is a hidden advantage held in reserve, US usage.

entries.clue: Senior ministers lodge ineffective complaint ultimately (7)

indicators.note: at the end, so take the final letters

blocks.note: last letters of ineffectivE and complainT

annotation.surface: Top ministers finally filing a toothless grievance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' reads as the verb in 'lodge a complaint'; it is the noun, a small house.
annotation.definitionFit: In British government the senior ministers meet as one body under the prime minister, and that body takes its name from a private room.

entries.clue: James reported error in part of school uniform (7)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so go by the sound

blocks.note: Jim's, as in James's, sounds like GYM'S

annotation.surface: A mistake by James in a school's uniform, as noted in a report.
annotation.walkthrough: Jim is short for James; the sound gives GYM, and the S joins it to SLIP. A gymslip is a sleeveless tunic worn by British schoolgirls.
annotation.definitionFit: A gymslip is a pinafore dress once standard in British girls' school uniform.

entries.clue: Do lovers ply Samaritan for change? (5,7)

indicators.note: the letters are exchanged into a new order

annotation.surface: Wondering whether lovers work on a Samaritan for spare coins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do' is not the verb but the noun, a party, so 'Do lovers' are people who love parties.
annotation.definitionFit: Party animals are people who love dos, or parties.

entries.clue: Strong in the future, say (7)

indicators.note: marks 'the future' as an example of a wider class, here a tense

blocks.note: the future is one grammatical tense

annotation.surface: A prediction that something will be powerful in time to come.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The future' reads as time ahead; here it is the grammatical future, one example of a tense.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: strong heat or strong feelings can both be described with the answer.

entries.clue: Republican ain’t travelling with queen in coach! (7)

indicators.note: letters on the move end up in a new order

annotation.surface: An anti-monarchist refusing to ride in the royal coach alongside the queen.
annotation.walkthrough: The republican shunning the queen's coach is the picture; 'coach' is the definition, a sports trainer, not a carriage.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sporting sense: the person who prepares a team or athlete, not the carriage the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Delay? Cockney bloke’s on time! (5)

indicators.note: Cockneys drop their initial H
in an across clue, placed after the previous piece

blocks.note: HARRY with the H dropped, as a Cockney says it

annotation.surface: Someone asking if there's a hold-up, told a Londoner has arrived punctually.
annotation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner, known for dropping H. Harry is just a stock bloke's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A slightly old-fashioned synonym, verb for verb: to linger or dawdle.

entries.clue: Splendid display of unlimited beer in kitchen cupboard (9)

indicators.note: with its limits, the first and last letters, removed
goes inside the next piece

blocks.note: a pantry is a food cupboard, split P…ANTRY
LAGER without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A fine show of endless beer stashed in the kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: P(AGE)ANTRY. 'Unlimited beer' sounds like a free bar; it means the beer word with its ends cut off.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the pomp of processions and ceremonies is a splendid display.

entries.clue: Group develop core tool for onboarding? (9)

blocks.note: the plank is the gym exercise for building core muscles

annotation.surface: A team building a key piece of software to bring new staff on board.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is office jargon: 'onboarding' new employees. The question mark signals it literally means getting on board a ship. PLANK comes from the fitness world, where planks build the core.
annotation.definitionFit: A gangplank is the board walked across to get on board a ship.

entries.clue: US peak — top it in style (2,7)

indicators.note: goes inside the next piece

annotation.surface: A climber urged to conquer an American summit with flair.
annotation.walkthrough: EL(CAP IT)AN. El Capitan is the huge granite cliff in Yosemite, famous among climbers.
annotation.definitionFit: El Capitan is a granite peak in Yosemite National Park, California.

entries.clue: V-sign from revolutionary very wrong after shelling (7)

indicators.note: once its shell, the outer letters, is removed

annotation.surface: A rude gesture from a revolutionary who's gone badly wrong after a bombardment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'V-sign' suggests the rude two-finger gesture; it is simply a V-shaped mark, as on a sergeant's sleeve.
annotation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe or symbol.

entries.clue: Drug injection, crack, taken casually (3,4)

annotation.surface: A list of drug use: a jab, crack cocaine, taken without care.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like another drug; it means an attempt, as in 'have a crack at'.
annotation.definitionFit: A potshot is a casual, random attempt or shot, a crack taken casually.

entries.clue: Benefit when including king in The Fifth Element? (5)

indicators.note: takes the next piece inside it

blocks.note: a boon = a benefit, split BO…ON

annotation.surface: A plus point of a king appearing in the sci-fi film The Fifth Element.
annotation.walkthrough: The Fifth Element is a 1997 film, but the question mark allows a literal reading: boron is element number 5 in the periodic table.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading of a film title: counting through the periodic table, atomic number 5 is this element.

entries.clue: In New York, drink case of beer that’s gross then go downhill (7)

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

blocks.note: to ski is to go downhill

annotation.surface: A New Yorker disgusted at a crate of beer, then everything going downhill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case of beer' reads as a crate of bottles; it means the letters casing the word BEER. Brewski is American slang for a beer.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: American slang for a beer, which 'In New York' flags.

entries.clue: Was monarch set on fire again after losing it? (7)

indicators.note: once it has lost the named piece

annotation.surface: Asking whether a king burned something again after misplacing it.
annotation.walkthrough: REIGNITED minus IT. 'It' looks like a pronoun for the fire; it is the two letters to delete.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to rule as king or queen.

entries.clue: Lacking a roof, hospital department cuts operations? (4-3)

indicators.note: cuts into, so it goes inside

blocks.note: two OPs, plural operations, split OP…OP

annotation.surface: A hospital department in a roofless building cutting back on surgery.
annotation.walkthrough: OP(ENT)OP. 'Operations' gives a pair of OPs, the plural spelt out as two copies.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective for buses and cars: the tourist bus with no upper deck roof is the classic example.

entries.clue: Shoot consumer inside shop and abscond (5)

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: An instruction to gun down a shopper in a store and run off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as fire a gun; it is a bamboo shoot, which pandas eat.
annotation.definitionFit: Pandas live on bamboo shoots, so a panda is a shoot consumer.

entries.clue: More expensive insurance payment? (7)

blocks.note: the regular payment on a policy

annotation.surface: A grumble that insurance is getting dearer.
annotation.walkthrough: Premium as an adjective means higher-priced; as a noun it is what you pay for insurance.
annotation.definitionFit: Premium means higher-priced and is also the payment for an insurance policy.

entries.clue: Bring home drinking article made of clay (7)

indicators.note: takes the next piece in, as a drinker takes in drink

blocks.note: to earn = to bring home (the bacon), split EAR…N

annotation.surface: Carrying home a pottery drinking vessel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drinking article' reads as a clay cup, which suits the definition; split it, and one word gives the instruction while the other is the grammatical article.
annotation.definitionFit: Earthen means made of baked clay, as earthenware.

entries.clue: Stadium hosting second large club (7)

indicators.note: a stadium hosting a match holds it within its walls, so ARENA holds S inside

annotation.surface: A stadium that is home to a second big football club.
annotation.walkthrough: AR(S)ENA + L. Arsenal is a London football club, and the stadium surface fits it neatly.
annotation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a football club in north London.

entries.clue: Obsessive personality playing English song dug out for the audience (3-5,4)

indicators.note: an audience hears it, so go by the sound

blocks.note: on = playing, as a song is on
mined = dug out, said like MIND

annotation.surface: A fixated fan playing an English song over and over for a crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a performer at a gig; 'dug out' is mined, as coal is, and only its sound is used.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who can think of only one subject is said to have this, which the clue calls an obsessive personality.
